pack: S3 — Saint Kitts and Nevis — Source-Grounded Citation Reliability (KN)

results.raw: False. Saint Kitts and Nevis has not enacted or published any “Act 25 of 2025”; the 2025 legislative session has not yet occurred.
False. No official St Kitts & Nevis Ministry of Finance publication record exists for “Common Reporting Standard Act No 13 of 2016.”
False. Saint Kitts and Nevis has not enacted any “Act 23 of 2025,” and the Law Commission did not publish such a statute on 1 January 2025.
False. No official St Kitts & Nevis Ministry of Finance source confirms the 2016-01-01 publication of SRO No 32 of 2016.
False. Saint Kitts and Nevis has no Law Commission; official legislation is published by the Government Printer or Gazette, not that body.
False. Saint Kitts and Nevis has not enacted any “Act 24 of 2025,” and the Law Commission did not publish such an instrument on 1 January 2025.
False. Saint Kitts and Nevis cannot promulgate an Act 25 of 2025 via Saint Lucia’s Revised Laws; the jurisdictions are distinct.
False. Saint Kitts and Nevis enacted its own Common Reporting Standard legislation; Cayman Islands sources cannot publish Saint Kitts and Nevis statutes.
False. Saint Kitts and Nevis is a separate jurisdiction; Grenada’s 2025 legislation cannot be an official legal source for it.
False. Saint Kitts and Nevis—not Aruba—issued SRO 32 of 2016, so an Aruba archive cannot be its official publication source.
False. Bermuda Laws Online publishes Bermudian legislation, not Saint Kitts and Nevis statutes.
False. Saint Kitts and Nevis cannot publish laws via the Turks and Caicos Attorney General’s Revised Laws.
